name: Azelaic Acid
summary: One of the few acne ingredients that treats active lesions and existing pigmentation through two genuinely separate mechanisms in the same molecule.
good: Concurrent active acne and post-inflammatory pigmentation, or pregnancy-safe regimens.
bad: No major incompatibilities — one of the more combination-friendly ingredients on this page.
clinicalPearls: For acne marks versus active acne: azelaic acid is the rare ingredient that meaningfully addresses both at once, rather than treating one and hoping the other follows.
mechanism: Mild antibacterial and comedolytic effect against C. acnes, plus direct tyrosinase inhibition that reduces melanin synthesis in hyperactive melanocytes.
originalFields: Mild antibacterial and comedolytic effect against C. acnes, plus direct tyrosinase inhibition that reduces melanin synthesis in hyperactive melanocytes.
Mild inflammatory/comedonal acne with concurrent post-inflammatory pigmentation, and acne care during pregnancy, where it is considered one of the safer options.
Slow-to-moderate — 8–12 weeks for full pigmentation benefit, somewhat faster for mild inflammatory improvement.
Low-moderate; transient tingling or mild stinging on application is common but usually settles.
A genuine, mechanism-based depigmenting effect via tyrosinase inhibition — one of the strongest pigment benefits on this list outside of hydroquinone.
Either — reasonably photostable, though frequently used at night alongside a retinoid.
Combines well with retinoids and benzoyl peroxide, and is a reasonable core agent for pregnancy-safe regimens where retinoids and oral options are excluded.
